business_model.claim: AII sells personal residential property insurance through its carrier subsidiary AIIC. Its customers are single-family homeowners and condominium owners, plus owners of vacant dwellings and investment properties. The business is predominantly in Florida, which was 91.1% of policies in-force at quarter end.
quotes: we provide personal residential property insurance for single- family homeowners and condominium owners, as well as coverage for vacant dwellings and investment properties, predominantly in Florida.
Florida represented 91.1% of our policies in-force as of September 30, 2026.

business_model.claim: AII runs a vertically integrated model and mainly writes in the 'Voluntary Market', where it chooses which risks to offer. That market was 75.5% of in-force premium at quarter end. Expansion states (South Carolina, Georgia and North Carolina) supported builder-agent relationships and were 6.9% of Voluntary Market in-force premium.
quotes: We employ a vertically integrated operating model whereby we control or manage substantially all aspects of insurance underwriting, actuarial analysis, pricing, distribution, and claims processing and adjudication.

As of September 30, 2026, 75.5% of our in-force premium was in the insurance market in which we underwrite and sell policies to policyholders where we choose to offer coverage without the assistance of residual market mechanisms

business_model.basis: stated in the cited item (annual report)
business_model.claim: Distribution runs through several channels: independent insurance agents, new-construction home builder agents, and national carriers that have restricted their Florida homeowners writing and refer business to AII.
quotes: We offer our insurance coverages through multiple distribution channels in the Voluntary Market, including independent insurance agents, new construction home builder agents, and national insurance carriers that have restricted their writing of residential homeowners insurance policies in Florida and refer business to us.

business_model.basis: stated in the cited items; the share of revenue is read from the income statement
business_model.claim: Revenue is mostly net premiums earned, which is gross premiums earned less premiums ceded to reinsurers. In the third quarter, net premiums earned were 101,161 of total revenues of 113,492 (table in thousands). Policy fees of 3,535 and net investment income of 8,415 (table in thousands) made up most of the rest.
quotes: We generate revenue primarily from insurance premiums earned, net of reinsurance ceded.

business_model.claim: Reinsurance is a large cost layer between gross and net revenue. AII ceded 60.4% of gross premiums earned in the nine months, down from 72.0% a year earlier. Ceded premiums earned fell to 439,971 from 472,275 (table in thousands) while gross premiums earned rose to 728,036 from 655,844 (table in thousands).
quotes: We ceded 60.4% and 72.0% of our gross premiums earned in the nine months ended September 30, 2026 and September 30, 2025, respectively.

business_model.basis: stated in the cited items; the expense comparison is read from the income statement
business_model.claim: A change in the quota share treaty shifted how premium and costs show up. AII cut the quota share cession rate from 40% to 25%. It therefore keeps more premium but receives less ceding commission, which raises policy acquisition and general and administrative expenses. Third-quarter policy acquisition expenses were 18,043 versus 6,254, and general and administrative expenses were 17,564 versus 7,347 (table in thousands).
quotes: Effective January 1, 2026, we reduced the percentage of our cession rate on our quota share reinsurance treaty from 40% to 25%, which impacted the comparability of our results between periods.

A lower cession rate increases the amount of premiums we retain on policies we write, and the reduction in the cession rate also reduces the ceding commission received on our quota share reinsurance treaty, which increases policy acquisition expenses and general and administrative expenses.

business_model.claim: Revenue growth is driven by policy count and premium written. Management cites voluntary new business of about 41,000 policies in the third quarter, up 57% year over year. Policies in-force reached 481,446, up 18.6% over the prior year. Gross premiums written were 293,299 versus 239,100 (table in thousands).
quotes: writing approximately 41,000 voluntary new business policies, an increase of 57% year over year
Policies in-force and in-force premium were 481,446 and $1,069 million, respectively, up 18.6% and 17.4%, respectively, over September 30, 2025

business_model.claim: Citizens take-outs are a secondary and shrinking growth source. AII assumed no Citizens policies in the third quarter because none met its standards, and it expects take-outs to be a smaller share of gross premiums written. Heavy take-out periods lower reported expense and loss ratios.
quotes: In 2026, we expect take-outs to be a smaller portion of our gross premiums written compared to 2024 and 2025.
As a result, periods of heavy take-out activity result in lower expense ratios and loss ratios.

business_model.claim: Loss costs are the main variable expense and swing with hurricane and named-storm activity from June 1 to November 30. Third-quarter net losses and loss adjustment expenses were 38,267 (table in thousands), a 36.6% loss ratio. That included net catastrophe losses of 5,064 (table in thousands).
quotes: This seasonality may result in significant variability in our losses and loss adjustment expenses (“LAE”) depending on the number, location and strength of hurricanes and other named storms during these months as compared to other months.

business_model.basis: stated in the cited items; the 15-20% figure is management's description in the second-quarter release
business_model.claim: The catastrophe reinsurance program renews each June 1 and is a major cost driver. Its pricing and terms materially influence results. quotes: Our reinsurance purchasing, including our catastrophe excess of loss reinsurance coverages, which commence on June 1st annually, also materially influences our financial results and is impacted by changes in reinsurance rates or alterations in terms and conditions, including in attachment or loss retention levels.
Successfully renewed 2026-2027 catastrophe excess of loss reinsurance program on June 1, 2026 with a risk- adjusted rate decrease at the upper end of 15-20% declines
